intro: To describe people's physical appearance and character, we use the verb ser. Today you learn to use adjectives and combine them with muy, bastante, and un poco.
b1.texto:
The verb **ser** is used to describe what someone is like on the outside and on the inside.

- Pablo **es alto** y **moreno**.
- Ana **es alta** y **simpática**.
- Lucía **es joven** e **inteligente**.

Many adjectives end in **-o** for masculine and **-a** for feminine: alto / alta, bajo / baja, simpático / simpática. Adjectives ending in **-e** or a consonant do not change for gender: un chico **inteligente**, una chica **inteligente**; un hombre **joven**, una mujer **joven**.

To qualify the description, we place words before the adjective:

- **muy** simpática (very)
- **bastante** alta (quite / rather)
- **un poco** baja (a little / a bit)
b2.f1.texto: She is tall, dark-haired and very friendly.
b2.f7.texto: The students are young and friendly.
b4.titulo: The adjective agrees with the person
b4.texto:
In Spanish, adjectives agree in gender (masculine or feminine) and number (singular or plural) with the person or thing they describe:

- Pablo is **alto**; Ana is **alta**.
- Pablo and Juan are **altos**; Ana and Lucía are **altas**.
- If the group is mixed, use masculine plural: ellos son **altos**.

Adjectives such as **inteligente** and **joven** change only in plural: inteligentes, jóvenes.
b6.pregunta: How do you say «she is very tall»?
b6.o0.refuerzo: Correct: «muy» goes before an adjective, and «alta» agrees in the feminine.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Incorrect: before an adjective, use «muy», never «mucho».
b6.o2.refuerzo: Incorrect: «alto» is masculine, and here we refer to a woman.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Correct: Ana is a woman, so we use the feminine form «alta».
b9.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «She is very friendly».
p.bajo.consejo: Masculine form for short height. The «j» sound is strong.
p.baja.consejo: Feminine form for short height: «una chica baja».
p.joven.consejo: Same for masculine and feminine. Plural: jóvenes.
p.simpático.consejo: Nice and friendly (masculine). Has an accent on the «á».
p.simpática.consejo: Nice and friendly (feminine). Has an accent on the «á».
p.inteligente.consejo: Ends in -e: same for masculine and feminine.
p.muy.consejo: Always placed before an adjective or adverb: «muy alta».
b5.f0.texto: Lucía and Pablo wait by the building door for their new flatmate.
b5.f1.texto: Pablo checks the picture on his phone and says that Ana looks very friendly, quite young and dark-haired.
b5.f2.texto: Lucía smiles and reminds him that in person people always change a bit, though the smile usually stays the same.
b5.f3.texto: When Ana steps out of the taxi with two large suitcases, she greets them with infectious warmth.
b5.f4.texto: She is tall, dresses simply and speaks in a calm, clear voice.
b5.f5.texto: In barely five minutes of chatting, the three walk up the stairs feeling that living together will be very pleasant.
p.estudiantes.consejo: Plural of «estudiante». The stress is on «dian», and the «d» between vowels is soft.
p.simpáticos.consejo: It comes from «simpatía». The «c» before «o» sounds like «k», and the stress is on «pá».
p.ellas.consejo: The «ll» sounds like «y», so say E-yas. Use it for a group made only of women or girls.
p.portal.consejo: Stress falls on the last syllable: por-TAL. Here it is the building entrance, not a website.
p.nueva.consejo: The «ue» is stressed here, so say NWE-ba. The «v» sounds like «b» in Spanish.
p.compañera.consejo: The «ñ» sounds like «ny» in «canyon». The «c» before «o» sounds like «k».
p.piso.consejo: It comes from «pisar». Very common in Spain. The stress is on «pi»: PI-so.
p.móvil.consejo: In Spain people say «el móvil» much more than «el teléfono». The stress is on «ó»: MO-bil.
p.persona.consejo: Used in «en persona» for meeting someone face to face. The stress is on «so»: per-SO-na.
p.cambia.consejo: Used with «la gente», which takes the singular form. The «ia» ending is quick: KAM-bya.
p.suele.consejo: Used to say what happens often. Stress on «sue», which sounds like «swe»: SWE-le.
p.misma.consejo: It agrees with a feminine noun, like «la sonrisa», so it ends in «-a». Stress on «mis».
p.taxi.consejo: The «x» sounds like «ks»: TAK-si. We say «el taxi», even though it ends in «i».
p.maletas.consejo: Plural of «maleta», which is feminine. The stress is on «le»: ma-LE-tas.
p.saluda.consejo: Same family as «saludo» and «saludable». The stress is on «lu»: sa-LU-da.
p.energía.consejo: The «g» before «i» sounds like «h». The accent mark on «í» shows the stress: e-ner-HI-a.
p.contagia.consejo: The «gi» sounds like «hi», and the final «ia» is quick: kon-TA-hya, stressed on «ta».
p.viste.consejo: The «v» sounds like «b»: BIS-te. Same family as «vestido» and «vestirse».
p.sencillez.consejo: From «sencillo», simple. Adding «-ez» turns it into a noun. The z sounds like the English th in thin.
p.minutos.consejo: Plural of «minuto». Stress falls on the «nu» in the middle, a clear mi-NU-tos, with a clear final o.
p.suben.consejo: From «subir», to go up. Its opposite is «bajar». The stress falls on «SU», the first syllable.
p.escaleras.consejo: From «escalera». The c before a sounds like a hard k: «es-ka-LE-ras», stress on «LE».
p.sintiendo.consejo: Gerund of «sentir». The stem vowel changes from e to i in this form, so it reads «sintiendo», not «sentiendo».
p.resultar.consejo: Shares the root of «resultado», result. Its first r is strong, like a rolled rr: rre-sul-TAR.
p.agradable.consejo: The «g» before «r» is soft and the stress falls on «DA»: «a-gra-DA-ble». Its ending «-ble» is the same in «posible».
